newsitem.title: UK: Novorossiisk berth two expected open by end Friday.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk berth two expected open by end Friday.

text.p: The last berth to reopen following an oil spill earlier this week at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk is expected to be back in operation by the end of Friday, a shipping source said.
Berth two, the port's second largest crude berth, remained closed on Friday morning as port officials cleaned up oil from the jetty after the spill last Tuesday.
"Two is still closed. They're struggling with oil underneath the jetty itself, but they have been pretty successful in mopping up what was there," said the source.
"We're hopeful that by the end of the day it will be open."
Nearly 400 tonnes of oil was spilled at the terminal on Tuesday night when a pipeline burst open, of which about 13 tonnes has spilled into the sea, the Russian Emergencies Ministry reported.

A crude tanker which was berthed at berth two when the accident occurred was still waiting to load on Friday, while another tanker was at anchor waiting to go into the berth which can accommodate tankers of up to 90,000 tonnes.
Berth six reopened on Thursday and a fuel oil tanker was loading on Friday.
Crude berths one and seven were not affected by the spill, while nothing was scheduled to load at the small products berth three.
The other Black Sea oil ports of Odessa and Tuapse and the Baltic port of Ventspils were operating normally on Friday.
